curator_notes: [Mechanistic Bridging -- model-generated hypothesis, not a tested result] Serine/glycine starvation (-SG medium; dietary serine/glycine depletion in vivo) induces a nrf2_ferroptosis signature (death_promoting) in HCT116 p53-/-; Erastin's reported resistance mechanism runs through the same pathway (GPX4-dependent lipid-peroxide detoxification). resistance_mechanism.mechanism_description: GPX4 detoxifies lipid peroxides downstream of cystine/glutathione depletion; sufficient GPX4 activity (or an intact glutathione pool feeding it) can rescue cells from erastin's system Xc- blockade despite cystine starvation (Dixon et al. 2012; Yang et al. 2014).

protocol_parameters.medium: MEM (21090) + 1x MEM vitamins (11120) + 10% dialysed FBS + 2 mM L-glutamine + 25 mM D-glucose; complete media additionally contains serine 0.4 mM and glycine 0.4 mM; starvation media omit both (-SG)

drug.name: Erastin

mechanism.raw_deg_evidence_ref: Maddocks et al. 2012 (PMID 23242140); p53-/- response per Figs. 1a-c and 3 (PMC6485472 full text)
mechanism.notes: p53-/- HCT116 cells fail the serine-starvation metabolic remodelling response: no protective p53-p21 arrest, oxidative stress, reduced viability and severely impaired proliferation; serine/glycine-depleted diet also significantly reduced p53-/- xenograft volume in vivo (translates to p53-deficient tumour vulnerability).
